- When sentiment is consistently negative (e.g., > 3 days of negative sentiment), reduce forecasted price by 1–2% relative to recent mean to avoid over-optimism.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), apply a 1–3 day lag correction: reduce forecast by 1–2% per day to reflect mean reversion.  
- If forecast is > 2% above recent 7-day average and sentiment is neutral or positive, reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overestimating bullish momentum.  
- If forecast is > 3% below recent 7-day average and sentiment is negative, increase forecast by 1–2% to avoid underestimating bearish momentum.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is consistently 1–2% below forecast, adjust future forecasts downward by 0.5–1% to reflect mean reversion bias.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated short-term reversals (e.g., +0.3 to -0.3 in 3–5 days), apply a 1–2 day smoothing filter to reduce forecast volatility.
